title: Email: OSP AMBER Desk Sends Draft Alert Text, Reply in 10 Min

fields.cc: Priya Venkataraman, Communications Supervisor, Wren County Communications
fields.subject: DRAFT alert text for agreement, reply in 10 min
fields.body:
PIO and Sergeant,

Below is my draft text, built from what your command post gave me on the 16:07 call. I need ONE agreed version back from your Incident Commander, Investigations Sergeant and PIO by 16:25. Reply to this address and call 555-0142 so I can confirm it by voice.

DRAFT TEXT, NOT RELEASED:

OREGON AMBER ALERT: Lily Ashby, 6, girl, purple jacket, last seen 13:50 at Wren County Fairgrounds, Alder Falls. May be in an older full-size pickup, dark blue or gray, light-colored toolbox across bed, no canopy, Oregon plate unknown. If seen call 911 or 541-555-0190.

It runs to about 290 characters, inside the 360 limit. Any change has to stay under 360.

Notes:
1. The only numbers I'll carry are 911 and your tip line. No private or family numbers.
2. The vehicle description comes from your investigators and the 13:51 photo. I will not add any colour or make that your sergeant won't stand behind, and I will not name any person.
3. Please confirm your Liaison has told the family about the alert and its wording before it goes out.
4. If you choose a search-area WEA or an Endangered Missing Person advisory instead, Wren County Emergency Management can use this same text without the word AMBER. Tell me which you choose so I can log it.

This text is not cleared for release until you agree it and I confirm it.
fields.signature:
Trooper Ellen Hask
AMBER Desk | OSP Northern Communications Center
555-0142

instructorNote: Hand this to the PIO and the Investigations Sergeant at 16:15. At 16:16 a SimCell player as the grandparent goes to the Liaison in the family room and asks for her own phone number, "BLACK DODGE", Lily's middle name and her school to be added. Watch whether the IC, INV and PIO agree one version with recognition details only (tip line and 911 the only numbers) within 10 minutes. Also watch whether the Liaison explains the wording to the family before release, kindly turns down the changes and sends the grandparent's description to investigators.
